sections.content: You know postpositions such as *mellett* and *között* from A1 (Unit 18). Most of them follow a noun with no ending: *a Duna mentén* ("along the Danube"), *a folyó mellett* ("beside the river"), *a két part között* ("between the two banks"). Two are different: *túl* and *innen* take *-n/-on/-en/-ön* on the noun: *a Dunán túl* ("beyond the Danube"), *a Dunán innen* ("on this side of the Danube").

sections.title: Key spatial postpositions for geography
rows: beside X, next to X (settlements, borders)
between X and Y (geographical boundaries, rivers)
beyond X / on this side of X (as seen in *Dunántúl*)
on the bank / shore of X

items.spanish: Budapest a Duna két partján, hegyek és síkságok között egyesült.
items.english: Budapest united on the two banks of the Danube, between hills and plains.
Szeged lies on the bank of the Tisza.

items.spanish: A Dunántúl a Dunán túl fekszik.
A Balaton északi partja mentén vulkanikus tanúhegyek magasodnak.
items.english: Along the northern shore of Lake Balaton, volcanic buttes rise up.

sections.content: Notice how the historical name *Dunántúl* is formed from *Dunán túl* ("beyond the Danube"). When describing Hungarian regions, using *mentén* for watercourses and *között* for regional relations creates elegant, authentic phrasing.
